scope: Close the residual Java getLevel(player/self/owner) frontier by inventorying every direct call and proving that none supplies player combat level as PRE-CU gameplay authority.

findings: Publish 14.1 player progression is skill-box and XP-pool based; player combat level is not an equipment, combat, profession, respec, pet, battlefield, or reward authority.
Retained creature, pet, encounter, target-dummy, and display-object levels remain valid content inputs when the object being measured is not a player.

The inherited NGE Java tree retains compatibility implementations, but player-capable level reads must be dominated by PRE-CU routing, a hard retirement boundary, or a central NGE-command denial before execution.

nonPlayerContentObject.authority: AI actors, pets, beasts, TCG barn displays, and target-dummy objects; self is not player progression authority.

precuBypassedCombatFallback.authority: The two action-cost overloads return through precuHamCostModel before level scaling, while all six defense fallbacks select a fixed player branch before the non-player level expression.

retiredProgression.authority: NGE respec, auto-level, live-conversion, and CTS profession restoration are fail-closed; two compatibility helpers containing level reads have no production caller.

retiredNgeCombat.authority: Bounty Hunter, Force Sensitive, Officer, Smuggler, and species NGE actions are denied to players by combatStandardAction before the level-bearing handler or its helper runs.

retiredRetainedContent.authority: Beast Master creation, player heavy-weapon DOT tiers, queued battlefields, and Officer supply drops return through their retirement boundaries before player or owner level is read.

dormantAdminDebug.authority: Legacy working scripts are absent from production template attachment; the only QA-listed script is God-level gated and self-detaches from non-admin players.
